# Cap a Daytona Process.Run timeout

Run `echo hello with timeout` with `Process.Run` / `sandbox.process.run` and a
whole-second `timeout` of five seconds. The program loads that sandbox with
`client.get`.

## What this means

A positive `timeout` caps this call. Values must be whole seconds
(`5 * time.Second` / `5000` ms). Omit or zero adds no extra client deadline and
no separate Daytona command limit (Daytona would otherwise default to 10
seconds).

## Edge cases

- `1500` ms / `1500 * time.Millisecond` is rejected before Daytona runs. The
  error field is `timeout`.
- Cancel the Go context (or abort the TypeScript call) to end the wait. The
  remote command may keep running; the handle stays busy until that provider
  call settles.

## Run

```sh
cd examples/go/daytona/process/run-daytona-with-timeout
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in the values below, then:
go run .
```

Requires Go 1.26.0+ and this checkout. Skip copying if `.env` already exists.
Local check: `GOWORK=off go test ./...`.

### Environment

```dotenv
DAYTONA_API_KEY=
DAYTONA_SANDBOX_ID=

# Optional Daytona endpoint and target overrides.
# DAYTONA_API_URL=https://app.daytona.io/api
# DAYTONA_TARGET=

```

## Warnings

- Needs an existing sandbox.
- Closing the handle leaves the sandbox as it is. Closing the client closes
  your connection to the provider.

Sessions, PTY, streaming handles, and Daytona `code_run` stay out of this cut. --- ## What changed (by layer) ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph contracts [Contracts] Proto["proto ExecOptions / ExecResult"] Inventory["specs/validation.yaml ExecOptions"] end subgraph core [Core SDKs] GoCore["Go sandbox.Process"] TSCore["TS sandbox.process"] Clone["Go cloneExecOptions / cloneExecResult"] end subgraph providers [Providers] DGo["Go Daytona"] DTS["TS Daytona"] MGo["Go Modal + stream close on cancel"] MTS["TS Modal"] end subgraph docs [Docs and site] Guide["docs/process.md + /docs/process"] Examples["24 process examples"] Site["Provider switch + home sample"] end Proto --> GoCore Proto --> TSCore Inventory --> GoCore Inventory --> TSCore GoCore --> Clone GoCore --> DGo GoCore --> MGo TSCore --> DTS TSCore --> MTS GoCore --> Guide TSCore --> Guide Guide --> Examples Guide --> Site ``` --- ## Call path ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant App participant Kit as Kit Process.Run participant Validate as Kit validation participant Adapter as Daytona or Modal adapter participant Native as Provider SDK App->>Kit: Run(argv|shell, cwd?, env?, timeout?) Kit->>Validate: argv XOR shell, blank shell after trim, absolute cwd alt invalid Validate-->>App: InvalidArgument (field set) else valid Kit->>Kit: operation deadline from timeout / client Kit->>Adapter: mapped request Adapter->>Adapter: whole-second timeout gate Adapter->>Native: executeCommand / sandbox.exec Native-->>Adapter: exit + streams Adapter-->>Kit: ExecResult Note over Kit: Go preserves empty env / empty stdout|stderr after clone Kit-->>App: ExecResult (nonzero exit is OK) end ``` --- ## Provider mapping ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph kit [Kit ExecOptions] Argv["argv"] Shell["shell"] Cwd["working_directory"] Env["environment"] Timeout["timeout"] end subgraph daytona [Daytona] DCmd["POSIX-quoted shell string"] DShell["shell as-is"] DExec["executeCommand"] DOut["stdout only; stderr empty"] DT0["timeout 0 when Kit omit/zero
avoids native 10s default"] end subgraph modal [Modal] MArgv["argv as-is"] MBash["bash -c shell"] MExec["sandbox.exec + drain pipes"] MOut["stdout + stderr"] MT0["Go Timeout 0 / TS omit timeoutMs
never send timeoutMs: 0"] end Argv --> DCmd --> DExec --> DOut Shell --> DShell --> DExec Timeout --> DT0 --> DExec Argv --> MArgv --> MExec --> MOut Shell --> MBash --> MExec Timeout --> MT0 --> MExec Cwd --> DExec Cwd --> MExec Env --> DExec Env --> MExec ``` | Kit input | Daytona | Modal | | --- | --- | --- | | `argv: ["echo", "hi"]` | POSIX-quoted shell string | argv as-is | | `shell: "echo hi"` | shell as-is | `["bash", "-c", "echo hi"]` | | omitted / zero timeout | command timeout `0` | no limit (TS omits `timeoutMs`; Go `Timeout: 0`) | | fractional timeout (`1500` ms) | rejected (`timeout`) | rejected (`timeout`) | | stderr | empty (Go: non-nil empty slice) | collected from pipe | | empty `environment` `{}` | Kit keeps explicit; TS native SDK may coerce to omit (same runtime: add no vars) | Kit keeps explicit | --- ## Review fixes in this branch ### 1. Go empty-collection cloning (bug fix) `proto.Clone` drops empty maps and empty byte slices. Process used the naive `cloneMessage`, so: - `Environment: map[string]string{}` became `nil` before the provider - Daytona `Stderr: []byte{}` (and empty stdout) became `nil` after return **Fix:** `cloneExecOptions` / `cloneExecResult` (same pattern as Create). Covered by unit + `Process.Run` tests. ```mermaid flowchart LR In["ExecOptions / ExecResult
empty env or []byte{}"] --> Clone["cloneExec*"] Clone --> Out["owned copy
empties preserved"] Out --> Provider["provider sees non-nil empty env"] Out --> Caller["caller sees non-nil empty stderr"] ``` ### 2. Go Modal cancel no longer hangs on stdio drain (bug fix) Modal wires exec stdout/stderr with `context.Background()` (and no stream deadline when command timeout is 0). Kit's `Wait(ctx)` respects cancel, but the old `collectProcess` still `wg.Wait()`'d on `io.ReadAll`, so a client deadline could leave the caller blocked until the remote process EOFs. **Fix:** on `Wait` failure, close stdout/stderr so blocked reads unblock (matches Modal's Close-unblocks-read contract), then return the wait error. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Kit as collectProcess participant Wait as process.Wait(ctx) participant Out as stdout/stderr ReadAll Kit->>Out: start drain goroutines Kit->>Wait: wait for exit Note over Wait: ctx canceled / deadline Wait-->>Kit: error Kit->>Out: Close streams Out-->>Kit: reads unblock Kit-->>Kit: return wait error ``` ### 3. Shared whole-second timeout helper `sdk.WholeSecondDuration` shared by Go Daytona and Modal adapters. Behavior unchanged: nil/zero → `0`; non-whole seconds rejected. ### 4. Docs honesty - Daytona omit/zero → always send `0` (native default is 10s) - Modal TS must omit `timeoutMs` (Modal rejects `0`) - TypeScript abort is **soft** on the remote side: Kit rejects the `await`; Daytona/Modal exec often ignore `AbortSignal` so the command may keep running. The handle still stays busy until that provider call settles (see §7). - Empty env wording matches runtime (incl. Daytona TS `{}` coerce) - `shell` blankness is after `TrimSpace` / `trim()` (whitespace-only fails); inventory comment matches ### 5. Daytona TypeScript process tests Covers argv POSIX quoting, omit/zero → `0`, cwd/env forwarding, fractional reject, empty stderr. ### 6. Small cleanups - Shared Go `absolutePath` for sandbox path + working directory - Modal `#file` → `#withSandbox` - Portable proto timeout comment + regenerated contracts; provider details stay in docs / Go alias ### 7. TypeScript handle serialization holds through in-flight abort (bug fix) Abort/timeout must reject the caller promptly, but the next lifecycle, filesystem, or process call on the **same** handle must not overlap native work that providers ignore mid-call. Matching Go and the documented one-at-a-time contract: 1. `#serialized` starts the provider promise (`work`) once the gate is acquired. 2. `awaitWithSignal(work, signal)` races that **already-started** promise so abort rejects without dropping it. 3. `finally` unlocks when `work` settles (not when the caller rejects), so a queued follow-up waits. while native still in flight"] end subgraph after [After: unlock when work settles] A1["acquire gate"] --> A2["work = body(signal)"] A2 --> A3["awaitWithSignal(work)"] A3 -->|"abort rejects caller"| A4["finally: unlock on work.then"] A4 --> A5["next call waits
until native settles"] end ``` Covered by client tests: aborted in-flight `start`, `process.run`, and `filesystem.readFile` keep `maximumActive === 1` until release. ### 8.
